AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.reason: Algebraic moduli is the general theory (projective parameter spaces, Hilbert and Quot schemes, algebraic spaces, stacks, coarse spaces, deformation comparisons, characteristic-zero resolution) that many roadmaps consume: abelian schemes, PEL and Shimura moduli, Faltings finiteness, local Galois deformation rings, K-theory and GAGA. It is not a continuation of Modular curves in that roadmap's own direction; ModularCurvesPartII already plays that role. By PROTOCOL section 15 a general theory that subsumes an existing roadmap's special cases builds on them: it keeps its place, imports what the anchors plan, and proves its general statements compatible with them. So it is kept, with eight layers narrowed.

AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.keeps: Projective bundles P(E) = Proj_S(Sym E) of a finite locally free module (and, over a Noetherian base, of a finite module) with O(1), O(n), the invertible-quotient universal property and base change, identified with the rank-one case of Modular curves 0G's relative Grassmannian and with StableReduction layer 2's relative Proj; the cohomology of O(n) on P(E); smoothness of Grassmannians and the Plücker closed immersion (0G states only projectivity and finite presentation); flag schemes, as closed subschemes of products of 0G's Grassmannians, with their universal flags; relative very ampleness and the projective embeddings it defines, on top of layer 2's relative ampleness; Hilbert polynomials, Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and the boundedness statements in the Noetherian setting its consumers use; the closedness of the Frobenius-stable (semilinear) lattice conditions used by R05 and LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, derived from 0G's closedness of invariant-subbundle equations; and the incidence and rank loci {dim(F ∩ W) ≥ k} in Grassmannians used by MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.
AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.reason: Modular curves 0G constructs the relative Grassmannian of locally free rank-N quotients of a finite locally free module, with affine charts, transition maps, gluing, universal property, base change and projectivity, and cuts out invariant-subbundle (Hopf-ideal) equations as closed loci. StableReduction layer 2 plans relative ampleness, projective morphisms and relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra. Tau Ceti roadmaps own what they plan, so R09.1 imports both and keeps what they do not plan.

AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.keeps: Hilbert and Quot schemes with fixed Hilbert polynomial in the projective finite-presentation cases used, realised inside the Grassmannians of Modular curves 0G through R09.1's boundedness, with representability, projectivity of the parameter morphism when the chosen theorem applies, base change, flatness of the universal family (not of H → S) and the dual-number negative example; relative Hom and Isom schemes of projective flat families through Hilbert schemes of graphs, proved to agree with Modular curves 0F's representable Hom functors from a finite locally free source; and the Chow-lemma/proper-modification and coherent dévissage package for proper GAGA.
AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.reason: Modular curves 0F owns the representable Hom functors from a finite locally free source (the affine Weil-restriction case) with base change, and 0G the Grassmannian in which parameter spaces are realised. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.keeps: Effective fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules on schemes: the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules and descent data along fpqc coverings, with full faithfulness and effectivity (Stacks 023T), its functoriality and its coherence with pullback, base change and tensor product, and the finite-type, finitely presented, coherent and finite locally free subclasses under the hypotheses stated in each result, built on the affine faithfully flat case that Mathlib already has (comonadicExtendScalars in Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Descent.lean, whose effective-descent corollary is still marked TODO there) and not on representability of sheaves of sets; quasi-coherent and coherent modules on algebraic spaces through étale presentations, with effective descent of coherent modules along étale presentations of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over a locally Noetherian base in the proper-GAGA setting consumed by ComplexComparisonPartII C3; the fpqc equivalence for arbitrary quasi-coherent modules above does not need a Noetherian hypothesis, and no unrestricted preservation of coherent modules by every base change is asserted; the comparison theorem that on the finite locally free and finite étale equivalence relations of Modular curves 0C, 4C and 9A the algebraic-space quotient of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1 is their scheme quotient (cited, not rebuilt); Weil restriction as an algebraic space along finite locally free morphisms for arbitrary targets, with the Stacks 05YC base-change map and 05YF representability, restricting to 0F in the affine case; and effective fppf descent for projective schemes of arbitrary relative dimension equipped with a relatively ample invertible sheaf, separating descent of the line bundle from descent of the object with that bundle, built on 0E's affine and finite cases and StableReduction layer 2's graded-algebra (relative Proj) method.
